note: Where every shipped source file under patches/ and extensions/ came from. A rule naming a single file wins over the directory rule around it; otherwise each file matches exactly one rule. A ported rule names the upstream repository, the commit it was copied from, the repositories it came through and its licence, and every file's header names a repository of its rule, by URL. Every upstream named here must also appear in NOTICE. ProvenanceTest checks all of it. A Facebook-family repository named here also has to be allowed by sources/facebook-sources.json: one files are ported from has to be adopted there, with this rule's commit, and one a rule credits has to be adopted or a candidate. scripts/test-facebook-sources.ps1 checks that side.

rules.license: GPL-3.0-only with the Morphe section 7 notices
rules.changes: Facebook host and id names in DiagnosticRedactor, Facebook wording in user-facing messages, HushfeedPause renamed HushfacebookPause with its keys and marker file, the extension name BundleVerifier expects. L10n moved from Hushfeed's TikTok extension into the shared library, with the en-XA and ar-XB pseudo-locales, lists joined and sentences capitalized in the text's own language, and the messages the shared settings screen shows read through it (Logger's debug toast stays English, for whoever reads the report). SettingsJson refuses a name given twice with an exception of its own. Changed files carry a 'Modified for Hushfacebook' line.
Rewritten for Facebook: package, both Meta signer digests, and the 577.0.0.50.72 arm64 target with its version code and floor as andrewliang25/morphe-patches declares it.

Rewritten from the source at that commit, not cherry-picked. Packages, extension descriptors, log tags, injected method names and the cache folder renamed; plain patch names with categories; the two feed guards merged into one shared hook; a settings switch in front of the story, reel, browser and download hooks, and the reel sidebar's Download button and the story menu's Save item asking theirs before they go in, so Pause takes both out; the player-source recorder shared with Download any video through a call and a switch of each patch's own; the save folder and its top folder read per file from the settings, the top folder with its MediaStore collection; the DASH track and the single file picked for the download quality read per save, by the track's own FBQualityLabel; a video named from the file name template, with the id the story's recorded player, the post or the reel's player params (their toString) gives; the list register of the story filter computed for static and wide parameters; the borrowed v0 in the reel collection hooks checked; the DASH join ends a track on an empty read and shifts both tracks by one lead-in; the reel handler answers null instead of Facebook's renamed kotlin.Unit, and sends the reel's link instead of saving it while links are sent, with a long press copying it; the debug println lines removed; the browser's link shim unwrapped only in the host and path forms Facebook 577 and 580 recognise as one themselves, plus /l.php on messenger.com, a shim inside a shim included. Saves fetch only what MediaUrlPolicy allows, every redirect included, into a cache file first, and reach MediaStore only once the declared type, the first bytes, the length and the 512 MB cap (the two DASH tracks together) all check out; save steps go to the diagnostic report without file names; a save reports its progress to a notification with a Cancel button and stops when cancelled, and lists its pending gallery row until it's settled. The story menu's save action is found among the types the menu creates, by the event it reports as a literal or as a string table entry, where Facebook 581 moved it. Andrew Liang credits FroggoMorphePatches for some ideas and implementations.

Rewritten from the two patches at that commit. The anchors are the same: the bumper component's constructor string and its one static (props) -> Z predicate, and the reel overlay enum's INTERESTED_OR_NOT_INTERESTED_BUMPER constant and the one (reel) -> Z method that reads it. Instead of returning false from the first instruction, each answer the predicate gives goes through an extension hook with a switch, so pausing Hushfacebook or turning a switch off brings the prompt back, and the diagnostic report counts the prompts kept out. Both are checked on 580 as well as 577, and a missing or doubled anchor stops patching with a message naming it.

Rewritten from the patch at that commit. The anchors are the same: the static Z predicate the reel overlay asks before adding its AFFILIATE_EYEBROW constant, the one string lookup the feed video plugin's isFooterHidden method makes, and the one static card reader of OrganicAffiliateFloatingCtaPlugin. Instead of returning false or null from the first instruction, each answer goes through an extension hook with a switch, so pausing Hushfacebook or turning the switch off brings the cards back, and the diagnostic report counts the cards kept out in each place. Checked on 580 as well as 577. On 580 the overlay's list builder is inlined into its render, and the same shape still matches once.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch behind Hide affiliate product links. The patch hands it each answer of the three places that ask whether a post has a product card (the reel overlay's predicate, the feed's footer id lookup and the comment sheet's card reader), and while the switch is on and Hushfacebook isn't paused it answers no or null, the answer for a post without a shop link. Any other time, and on any throw, Facebook's own answer stands.
Written for Hushfacebook: which addresses a save may fetch (HTTPS on 443, no user name, Meta's media CDNs only, and on a direct route a public or fake-IP answer).

Written for Hushfacebook: Download to phone in the menu of a feed or Watch video, added after Facebook fills the menu so its own Save and Download rows stay as they are, found in Facebook 577 and 580 through the video feed menu's log tag, the kept GraphQL models and the hashes of their field names; the save folder, one sanitized folder name under the top folder Save to picks, Movies and Pictures, DCIM or Download, each written through the MediaStore collection Android allows there; the download quality, the ceiling a save holds the DASH track and the single file to, falling back to the nearest above it; and the video file name, a template with {date}, {video_id}, {owner} and {posted} cleaned like the folder name, kept off the photo prefix, a typed extension and one name for every save, and bounded in bytes, with the poster and the post day read off every model's kept TreeJNI accessors by the hash of the field's GraphQL name, from the reel's story, which the reel sidebar hands its assembly call, the story card's own tree, found by the card's kept getTimestamp, and the post and media a video's menu holds; and a Download that sends the reel's or the video's facebook.com link, built from its id alone, to a named app or Android's chooser instead of saving it.

Written for Hushfacebook: the tracking keys Facebook adds to shared and opened links, taken out offline with everything else in the link left as written, and the hooks on the methods of Facebook 577 and 580 that add them.

Written for Hushfacebook: Start on x86 devices, which adds Facebook's MprotectCode start-up task and its later half to the list of start-up tasks Facebook's own cold start experiments skip, on an x86 device running Facebook's arm code translated, found in Facebook 577 and 580 through the log line that names that list.

Written for Hushfacebook: the rule that hides feed posts Facebook's own detection marked as made with AI. The idea follows the Facebook 573 AI filter of FroggoMorphePatches, which ArunTS96/FroggoMorphePatches and mben25/morphe-patches carry too. No code of it is here: that filter writes down 573's obfuscated names, while this finds GraphQLStory's accessor in 577 and 580 by the schema keys it loads, holds it to the flag Facebook's own GenAiTransparencyPlugin reads, and reads the flag through kept members. The opt-in creator label switch reads the plugin's second flag, was_self_disclosed_as_ai_generated, through GraphQLStory's self-disclosure accessor, found and held the same way.

Written for Hushfacebook: the Material You theme. Dark-mode colours move to the wallpaper palette (Android 12 and newer) or to a fixed tonal palette of Facebook's blue (Android 11) at the same lightness, through the four colour routes the AMOLED patch uses and after it, and through night copies of Facebook's dark FDS styles for the views it inflates from its own layouts. React Native screens such as Marketplace home, whose colours come from their JavaScript, go through React's own background, border and image tint setters and its text colour span, which both themes hook. The colour tokens and dark surfaces it recolours were read off Facebook's own light and dark themes in the 577 and 580 builds, not taken from another patch source.

Written for Hushfacebook: Facebook's own answer to whether its dark mode is on, kept from each answer its dark mode controller gives. Both themes ask it, since the Video tab stays dark in light mode with the same colours dark mode uses.

Written for Hushfacebook: Force dark mode, a switch that has Facebook's dark mode controller answer dark whatever its own setting says, for tablets whose Facebook settings have no Dark mode row (issue #64).
Generated for Hushfacebook by scripts/gen-l10n.py from its own translation tables in extensions/shared/library/src/main/l10n.

Written for Hushfacebook: a running save's notification with its progress and a Cancel button, the removal of the work files and pending gallery rows a save left when Android ended the process, and the MP4 writer that joins a DASH picture and its sound for the formats MediaMuxer won't write, VP9 always and AV1 before Android 14, by copying the fragments' boxes and samples into one plain MP4.

Ported from Hushfeed's settings backup and cut down to what Hushfacebook keeps: an exact list of its feature switches and the save folder in place of every setting, with no Feature Gate Lab, reset, undo or journal. An import is read into a snapshot that a preview shows before anything is written, and applied in one preference commit. A file declaring a newer version, a name given twice, a switch that isn't true or false, a folder that isn't one clean folder name, or more than 64 KB changes nothing, each with its own reason, and names this build doesn't know are counted rather than applied.

Ported from Hushfeed's backup rows: Export settings and Import settings on the framework preference page inside Hushfacebook's settings dialog, answered through the page's onActivityResult, with the import's preview dialog kept in the page's saved state so it comes back after the activity is rebuilt. No Reset or Undo rows, and every message read from L10n.

Written for Hushfacebook: the shared feed hook and filter (the chokepoint and getters follow andrewliang25/morphe-patches, the PROMOTION rule follows FroggoMorphePatches), the extension context hook, the settings switches and status flags, and the launcher-shortcut settings screen built the way Hushfeed's settings are. The screen's opt-in release check, which asks api.github.com for the latest Hushfacebook release, was written here too.
Written for Hushfacebook: a Story progress-completion guard on Facebook 577 and 580 that leaves manual navigation alone.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch on the report of viewed stories that Facebook's story viewer sends as DirectSeenMutation, which puts the viewer on a story's viewer list. The patch finds the mutation's query class in Facebook 577 and 580 by its name and root field, the one method that creates it and fills story_ids_list, and the one other method of that class that calls it, and asks the extension first thing in that sender, which returns without sending while the switch is on. Loukious/FacebookAppAdsRemover and gnadgnaoh/NexAlloy-XES offer the same feature; neither is licensed for reuse, so nothing was taken from them.

Written for Hushfacebook: the Reels viewer clean-up, which drops the chips under a reel by their GraphQL type, answers Facebook's own Follow check and its config for removing the Following button, and skips the footer's hot comment and friends' reaction queries, each behind its own switch, with the hooks found in Facebook 577 and 580 by kept literals and Redex names.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch on Facebook's own update prompts. Facebook 577 and 580 carry no installer of their own, so the patch fails the two QuickPromotion filters that ask Meta App Manager about updates, skips the push handler that has the manager look for one, and fails the chat promotion filter aimed at versions below a ceiling, each found by its shape and the literals it keeps.

Written for Hushfacebook: the font swap. It stands at the exit of the typeface repository's resolver, found in Facebook 577 and 580 by the refusal it throws for a family with no source, at the exit of the variable-font builders the kept com.meta.foa.typefacebuilder.ApiUtils makes, and at the exit of React Native's typeface resolver, found by the variation settings refusal its utilities log, at the exit of Facebook's own Roboto builder, found by the message it logs when it can't make one, and at each read of Android's default typefaces in Facebook's code. It answers the phone's default font, or a font file picked in the settings and copied into Facebook's files after a check, at the same weight and slant, for Meta's interface families only, which it knows by the enum constant names Redex keeps and by the family names React Native screens ask for. At the Roboto builder and the default typeface reads it answers a picked file only, since both are the phone's font already.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch on the batches of watched reels Facebook's Reels viewer sends as FbShortsSeenStateMutation. The patch finds the batcher's flush in Facebook 577 and 580 by the mutation's name, its video_ids input and the Redex name of the runnable it hands its executor, and puts the extension in place of that hand-over. The extension holds a batch back while the switch is on and sends anything it doesn't recognise as Facebook handed it over.

Written for Hushfacebook: the rename that lets Meta's own apps install beside a re-signed Facebook. It renames the two signature permissions Facebook shares with Messenger, Lite, Business Suite and Workplace, com.facebook.permission.prod.FB_APP_COMMUNICATION and com.facebook.receiver.permission.ACCESS, to app.hushfacebook. names in every place the manifest names them, and hands every literal Facebook's code loads for them to an extension that answers the name the install holds. Messenger-Z's notes on the collision were read for the behavior only; no code came from them.

Written for Hushfacebook: the anchors and stub fills behind the Debug logging test of a same-key Messenger's link, which finds Facebook's message expiration flag reader and one of its Context-to-session lookups on Facebook 577 and 580 and has the extension call them on request.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch to the phone's emoji font. It asks the extension first thing in Facebook's emoji typeface provider, found in Facebook 577 and 580 by the end-to-end system emoji flag and the log tag it keeps, and hands back the phone's default typeface while the switch is on, so the spans and pickers that draw emoji with Meta's downloaded font draw the phone's emoji font instead. It also asks the extension first thing in the maker of Meta's emoji picture addresses, found by the picture base address it holds, and answers no address while the switch is on, so a chat's big emoji stays drawn with the provider's typeface instead of Meta's PNG.

Written for Hushfacebook: the tab Facebook opens on. The patch checks that Facebook 577 and 580 still pick the main screen's start tab from an intent's target_tab_id, by the one method that answers a tab id from that extra, and puts the extension first in the onCreate the main screen inherits. For a start from the launcher icon with nothing to restore, the extension hands the screen a copy of its intent asking for the chosen tab's id, the id each kept TabTag subclass hands TabTag, and leaves links, notifications, shortcuts and restored screens alone. Marketplace only is written here too: it asks the extension right after Facebook's hidden-tab set answers for each configured tab, in the one static method that builds the tab bar's shown tabs from NavigationConfig's list, so Home, Video, Friends, Feeds, Groups, Gaming and Events go the way a tab hidden in Facebook's own editor does. Hide the Reels tab is written here too: it shares that one call, a tab bar filter both patches depend on, and drops only WatchTab, the one TabTag class 577 and 580 keep for the tab accounts call Reels or Video, leaving a tab Facebook's own set already hides to Facebook. A start sent to the hidden tab asks for Home instead. Tab bar at the bottom is written here too: in 577 and 580 a static field set from fb4a_bottom_tabs_override_enabled holds the key of Facebook's own override of where the tab bar goes, and each method that reads it from FbSharedPreferences as a TriState and takes its ordinal gets a call right after the ordinal, which answers YES's ordinal while the switch is on. A load of the key that goes into anything else, Facebook's tab menu writing it, is left alone. No read, a read that answers no TriState or takes no ordinal right away, or a jump to the instruction after the ordinal stops patching with a message.

Written for Hushfacebook: the Get Messenger card in Facebook's own Chats. Facebook 577 and 580 build the rows above the chat list from plugins that each answer whether they show, and the card's plugin is found by the one builder that tags its banner mib-native-dismissible-top-banner. Facebook already leaves the card out when Messenger is installed, but only for a Messenger isSameSignature matches with its own key, which a re-signed build never does. The patch asks the extension first in that plugin's show question, and the extension answers no while the switch is on and com.facebook.orca is installed and enabled, whatever key signed it. Open Messenger from the top bar is written here too: the top bar's Messenger icon taps through one static method, the only one in 577 and 580 loading both entry_point_navbar_global_icon_ and entry_point_navbar_global_icon_reels_tab, which can hand the tap to a shared static Messenger button handler, the one static method of its shape loading long_press. The patch asks the extension first in both, and the extension starts Messenger's launcher entry for a plain tap while the switch is on and Messenger is installed.

Written for Hushfacebook: tap to play. The patch finds FbGrootPlayer's play, its inner pause and its bind in Facebook 577 and 580 by the trace strings they keep, the older Rich Video Player's playback controller by its play and pause log lines, Facebook's Autoplay settings checker by the refusal its constructor names it in, and FbFragmentActivity's touch dispatch by its framework name. The extension holds a start unless the player is already playing something a tap started, the start's EventTriggerType is one only something you did sends, or a tap ended within a second and the trigger isn't one Facebook sends because something came into view or came back. The Autoplay setting reads Off while the switch is on, and nothing is written to it.

Written for Hushfacebook: the Upgrades and Also from Meta sections of Facebook's Menu. Facebook 577 and 580 type each Menu group with one enum under kept names, UPSELL and PRODUCTS_FROM_FACEBOOK among them, and build every group from a native section and a section for what the server sends with it. The patch finds the first by the one children builder loading upsell_bookmarks_key and the second by the one loading ABOVE_NATIVE, REPLACE_NATIVE and BELOW_NATIVE, and asks the extension about the group right after each reads it. A yes hands back an empty list of children, built the way the section builds its own. Each group has its own switch, and every other group is left as Facebook built it. The same folder holds Hushfacebook in the Menu: the Settings and privacy group's row list, the one list the native section builds from the session, a list and a flag, goes through the extension, which adds one row made by a factory the patch adds to Facebook's row item class, copying the first row's icon and giving it an id of its own. The Menu's row tap handler, found by the bookmarks_menu trace, opens the settings for that id, and its two loggers skip it.

Written for Hushfacebook: Meta AI in Facebook's search. On Facebook 577 and 580 the patch finds three of Facebook's own decisions from kept names and literals. The results page's question of whether to add a Meta AI answer is the one boolean over FbUserSession and SearchResultsMutableContext that both callers of the meta_ai_answer_entities page builder ask first, and the patch answers no there. A page of results is built by one constructor from a list of result modules, whose role is a constant of the enum Facebook loads where it logs a failed GraphQLGraphSearchResultRole parse, and the extension leaves out Meta AI's answer and prompt roles (SEARCH_META_AI_ANSWER with its body, full body and loading state, HCM_SEARCH_META_AI_ANSWER, HCM_RELATED_META_AI_PROMPTS with its loading state, and HCM_SEARCH_AI_MODE) and keeps every other role. The page's name comes along, so the Meta AI tab's own page, the one its builder names search_meta_ai_answer_module, keeps its answer. A suggestion's flag to open Meta AI is the boolean the results router asks GraphSearchQuerySpec before it sends a search to META_AI_TAB, and the patch hands it to the extension where the suggestion parser stores it from the server's reply. The Meta AI button and the results page's Meta AI tab go around all three.

Written for Hushfacebook: the order comments open in. Facebook 577 and 580 build every request for a post's comments from FetchFeedbackParams, and the request's builder sets comment_rendering_intent_token from one of its strings only when it isn't empty, so an ordinary comment sheet leaves the order to Facebook's servers. The patch finds that builder by the three variable names it reads from the params (comment_rendering_intent_token, feedback_id and focused_comment_id), finds the one params constructor that stores those three from its own parameters, and asks the extension first there. It also tells the extension first in the comment sheet's pick handler, the one method taking the session and a token that fetches UpdateCommentOrderType_FetchFeedbackQuery. The extension fills in RANKED_FILTERED_INTENT_V1, RECENT_ACTIVITY_INTENT_V1 or RANKED_UNFILTERED_CHRONOLOGICAL_REPLIES_INTENT_V1 only for a request that names no order and no focused comment, and asks again for the order picked in a post's menu until Facebook restarts.

Written for Hushfacebook: the ads in search results and on profiles. In Facebook 577 and 580 every page of search results is built by one constructor from the two builders that take a GraphQLResult and the search's SearchResultsMutableContext, and its module list is the parameter they fill with the module class's own list converter. The module class is the one holding the search result role enum it reads from result_role, and its static initializer keeps the enum's SEARCH_ADS, DEPENDENT_SEARCH_ADS, LATE_DEPENDENT_SEARCH_ADS and TOP_POSITION_SEARCH_ADS as its ads. The extension leaves a module out of the page when its role is one of those or one of the five other roles the enum names after ads. On a profile, the one method holding sponsored_timeline_stories_test_key is the timeline story component's render, which asks GraphQLStory for its sponsored_data; the extension has it draw nothing for a story that carries it.

Written for Hushfacebook: the People you may know carousel on your own profile. In Facebook 577 and 580 it is one Litho section that hands the name ProfilePeopleYouMayKnowSection to the section base class, and the profile's root section adds it only when the profile is the viewer's. The patch finds the one children builder loading that name, holds it to the section's constructor, to the base class's getLogTag() and setChildren of the builder's Children type, and to that type's public empty constructor and getChildren(), and asks the extension first there. The extension reads the name back through getLogTag() and has the builder hand back an empty Children while the People you may know switch is on.

Written for Hushfacebook: the reel ads Facebook builds as ordinary reels. In Facebook 577 and 580 the reel ad item's base class has one no-argument getter for its GraphQLStory, declared on one public interface up its supertypes that every reel item implements. The patch finds that interface and GraphQLStory's one sponsored_data accessor, and fills three extension stubs with them: whether an object is a reel item, the item's story, and the story's sponsored data. The extension drops a reel whose story carries sponsored data, the check Facebook's own Reels code makes before it shows a promotion over a reel.

Written for Hushfacebook: the kinds of push notification a user picks. Facebook 577 and 580 parse each push into the kept SystemTrayNotification, whose mType holds the payload's type, and read that type as a constant name of the kept NotificationType enum, before the first colon and ignoring case. Every push is posted through the one method of the kept SystemTrayNotificationManager that loads show_notif_start. The patch finds it by that literal and its kept parameter types, reads mType from the push its builder holds, and returns before anything is posted when the extension says the kind is blocked. Twelve kinds sit under six switches that all start off, and every other kind posts as Facebook posts it.

Written for Hushfacebook: the stories Facebook suggests in the Stories tray. In Facebook 577 and 580 every answer of the tray's fetch goes through the one method holding StoriesTrayLightFetchControllerQueryOps.postProcessResult, which hands the buckets as an ImmutableList to the one constructor of the tray data class it answers, and the classic tray's receiver, the one method holding optimistic_data_adapter_receives, reads that list. The patch goes first in that constructor and hands the list to the extension, which leaves out a bucket whose is_story_bucket_suggested flag is true or whose first label is SUGGESTED, the two things the tray's card reads before it writes Suggested. The flag is read through the bucket interface method the receiver calls and a tree class answers with that field's key, and the label through the one static helper answering the label enum, which also names NEWFRIEND and TRENDING, for that interface. Every other bucket and anything that isn't a bucket stays.

Written for Hushfacebook: the ads in Marketplace's feed. Facebook 577 and 580 draw Marketplace with React Native, and its Relay queries go out through Facebook's own Networking module, whose sendRequest is the one method holding FBNetworkingModule_React_Native. It reads a POST body from the request data's string entry into a StringEntity, and the query's tracking name (RelayFBNetwork_ and the query's name) from the same data. The patch hands the body and the data to the extension right after that read. For a Marketplace query whose form-encoded variables name shouldSkipAdRequest or shouldSkipBoostedListingAdRequest at their top level as false or null, the extension sets them to true and changes nothing else. For the four ads-only queries Facebook's own Tigon callbacks list (MarketplaceHomeFeedAdsQueryRendererQuery, MarketplaceHomeFeedAdsPaginationQuery, MarketplaceHomeFeedBoostedListingAdsQuery and MarketplaceHomeFeedBoostedListingAdsPaginationQuery) it answers no body, which the module reports to JavaScript as a request it couldn't make. Marketplace search's results query names neither variable and has no ads-only query, so its ads come back among the listings. The module's answers reach JavaScript through the kept FBTigonRequest$FBTigonCallbacks: onBody hands each piece of text, a toString() result, to React Native's didReceiveNetworkIncrementalData emitter and onEOM hands a whole one to didReceiveNetworkData, each with the request's state at hand, which sendRequest builds with the tracking name in one String field. The patch reads that field and hands the text, the name and the state to the extension right where the text lands. For a Marketplace query with Search in its name, other than the typeahead and mutations, the extension reads each whole JSON payload and takes out a result whose node's type ends in AdStory or that carries a sponsored_data object with an ad id, moving later streamed and deferred indices of its list down past the ads taken out. A streamed ad gives way to a payload with null data that keeps its extensions. A payload that fails to be read goes on as it came, and after it nothing more is taken out while later indices still move. Right before onEOM reports an answer complete through didCompleteNetworkResponse, the patch asks the extension for text still waiting for a payload to finish and hands it to the incremental emitter as one last piece.

Written for Hushfacebook: hiding feed posts by words the person lists. In Facebook 577 and 580 GraphQLStory has one accessor that asks getCachedModel for the field keyed message as the type tagged TextWithEntities, and GraphQLStory's own toString calls it, labels its text message.text and reads that with a static helper that is getCachedString of the key text. The patch finds that accessor and the one of attached_story as Story by their keys, holds the first to toString's reading, and fills two stubs in PostText with them. The rule runs in the shared feed guard: the extension reads both texts through the kept getCachedString after checking the model's type tag, folds them and the two bounded phrase lists with NFKC case folding, lets a keep phrase win, keeps any post whose text it can't read, and reports only counts.

Written for Hushfacebook: hiding the row of Meta AI questions under posts. In Facebook 577 and 580 one static method loads both DeepDivePillSocket and the kept class name of GenAiDeepDivePillPlugin. It loads every pill plugin's class name into one register and asks a static (model, index) -> Z check of its own class whether that plugin applies, twice per plugin, each answer in a move-result. The patch puts a call after each answer that hands the extension the answer and the name, and the extension answers no for Meta AI's plugin while its switch is on, so the socket goes on to the next plugin. A missing or doubled socket, plugin names in more than one register, or a register past v15 stops patching with a message.

Written for Hushfacebook: keeping the date on post headers. In Facebook 577 and 580 one method, the render of the post header subtitle that names itself FDSPostHeaderSubtitle, loads both in_cycling_experiment and subtitle_cycling_text_count. It works out whether the header rotates its subtitle, logs that boolean as in_cycling_experiment through String.valueOf right after the call that answers it, and then branches on it between a component that rotates the subtitle plugins' texts and the one line with the date. The patch finds that method by the two strings, checks the log's shape, and hands the answer to the extension at the log's own label, which answers no while the switch is on.

Written for Hushfacebook: the Feeds tab without its header. In Facebook 577 and 580 the Feeds tab is com.facebook.feed.fragment.FeedFiltersFragment, which keeps its member names. Its shouldInitializeNavBar answers whether the tab's chrome builds a title row, and the patch hands each answer to the extension at the return's own label, which answers no while the switch is on. Its onCreateView hands the container kept in tabBarContainer to the controller that fills and shows the filters. Right before that controller's new-instance the patch asks the extension, and on a yes puts a new container of the field's type in that register, built from the old one's Context the way the fragment builds its own, so the controller fills one that's never on screen. The fragment's feedFiltersFragmentContainerController posts a runnable Redex still names FeedFiltersFragmentContainerController$setViewPagerTopMargin$1, whose run() sets the posts' top margin to the filters' height when its boolean says they show. The patch hands that boolean to the extension between the read and the branch on it, and the extension answers no for a tab whose filters went to the container that's never on screen, so the posts start at the top.

Written for Hushfacebook: the people Facebook offers to tag while you write. In Facebook 577 and 580 every text box that can tag people is one AutoCompleteTextView subclass, found by the one performFiltering(CharSequence, int) that logs ImplicitMentionsCommonWordsFilter: JSON Parsing Exception. Right after it compares the first character of the word at the cursor with @, it reads a boolean of its MentionsAutoCompleteBehavior and returns before any lookup when the boolean is set, and both of those branches land on the lookup. The patch hands that boolean and the box (the behaviour's one field typed as the box's class) to the extension right after the read and keeps the answer in the same register. The extension answers yes while its switch is on, and closes a list of people left open by an earlier @. Words starting with @ or # never reach that read.

Written for Hushfacebook: resume long videos. FacebookAppAdsRemover describes the behavior and has no licence, so nothing was taken from its code. The patch finds FbGrootPlayer in Facebook 577 and 580 by its play trace, then its kept-name maybeTrackVideoStart and maybeTrackVideoStop, its release, bind and static seek by the trace strings they keep, its public seek as the one that hands on to that seek, its position reader as the one int method of the interface that declares isPlaying, and its length reader as the other int method its own remaining-time sum asks. VideoPlayerParams' field names come from the debug dump that reports each under its real name. The extension saves where a video longer than two minutes stopped, up to 200 of them for 30 days in a preferences file of its own, forgets one stopped near its end, and seeks back once on the video's next first start unless a seek came first or Facebook placed the start itself.

Written for Hushfacebook: the switch on liking a reel or a video with a double tap. The patch finds, in Facebook 577 and 580, the reel like helper by its kept trace FbShortsMutationUtil.mutateViewerLikeReaction, its double-tap like as its one instance method taking two objects and a boolean, GestureReactionComponent by the name its constructor gives it, that component's gesture view through onCreateMountContent, the view's heart by the shortFormVideoUnit key it logs, and the feed attachment's own double tap as the one onDoubleTap animating translationY. It hands the extension the gesture view's double-tap handler after every read of it, the double-tap like's key for the reel, the helper like's source and the attachment's double tap. While the switch is on the extension answers that there's no handler and no key, holds back a like whose source is DOUBLE_TAP and leaves the attachment's double tap unhandled, and otherwise hands back what Facebook handed over.

Written for Hushfacebook: keep the reel speed. The patch finds, in Facebook 577 and 580, FbGrootPlayer by its play trace, then its speed setter as the one instance (F)V method reading HeroPlayerSetting.enableLastPlaybackSpeedCacheUpdate, its PlayerOrigin getter as the one method answering a PlayerOrigin, its bind by its bindVideoSources trace and its kept-name maybeTrackVideoStart, and the Reels menu's speed toast as the one static (Context, float) method holding InlinePlaybackSpeedAttributeSelector. The setter, the bind, the start and the toast hand the extension their arguments first thing, and the extension's stubs are filled with the setter and the origin getter. The extension keeps a speed picked in the Reels menu, in memory only, with the origin of the player it was set on, and sets it on the first start after each bind of a player with that origin.

Written for Hushfacebook: hold a reel for 2x, using the hold-to-speed-up Facebook's Reels controls already have behind server flags. The patch finds, in Facebook 577 and 580, the long-press handlers as the lambdas keeping $shouldDispatchLongPressEventDirectly and $immersiveFeedPlayerConfig and holding "speed_up", the release listeners as the lambdas keeping $isInLongPress2xPlaybackSpeed and that config, the speed-up flag as the one flag the handlers ask the config, the release flag as the one the listeners ask straight before it, the renders of FbShortsVideoControlComponent and FbShortsViewerOverlayComponent that make those lambdas, the edge check as the one method of its shape the handlers call, and FbFragmentActivity.dispatchTouchEvent. Each flag answer the handlers, the listeners and the renders take, and each answer of the edge check, goes through the extension, which says yes while the switch is on, the listeners' yes only until a lift they hear after a hold, which it tells from the touches it reads. The hold speed both speed-ups read goes through the extension too, which makes one no faster than normal 2x. FbGrootPlayer's speed setter hands the extension the player and the speed first thing and goes on with the speed it answers, and the extension's stub is filled with the player's speed getter, the one the listeners read, so a hold's lift puts back the speed the reel played at before the hold.

Written for Hushfacebook: the quality videos play at, an idea De-Vanced also has, written from Facebook's own code. The patch finds, in Facebook 577 and 580, the DASH format evaluator as the class of the one (String)V call in the method holding HeroServicePlayer.setCustomQualityInternal, built with an AbrContextAwareConfiguration; that custom-quality setter's array of tracks and the static method and field it reads a track's label with; and the String field the evaluator hands its own setter at its first choice, its preselected label. The setter asks the extension first with its label, the constructor tells it about the evaluator before each return, and the extension's stubs are filled with the preselected label, the tracks and a track's label. While the switch is on and a quality is chosen, the extension leaves a marker as the preselected label of an evaluator Facebook gave none, and turns it into the label of the track the chosen quality plays when the setter gets it.
